issues.claim: a 17-year-old FreeBSD remote code execution vulnerability designated CVE-2026-4747
issues.issue: CVE-2026-4747 is a FreeBSD RPCSEC_GSS kernel RCE, but does not appear to be '17-year-old.' The '27-year-old' long-lived vulnerability highlighted by Anthropic was in OpenBSD, not FreeBSD. The report conflates the FreeBSD CVE with the OpenBSD longevity claim.
issues.suggested_fix: Separate: (a) CVE-2026-4747 is a FreeBSD RPCSEC_GSS kernel RCE discovered via Mythos (FreeBSD advisory March 26, 2026); (b) Mythos separately found a 27-year-old vulnerability in OpenBSD. Remove the '17-year-old' age attribution from the FreeBSD CVE.

issues.claim: Project Glasswing founding participants: Amazon, Anthropic, Apple, Broadcom, Cisco, CrowdStrike, The Linux Foundation, Microsoft, Palo Alto Networks
issues.issue: Multiple independent sources (VentureBeat, CNBC, Motley Fool, CyberScoop) list additional major partners including Google, Nvidia, and JPMorganChase. Additionally, listing 'Anthropic' as a founding partner is misleading since Anthropic is the organizer/convener.
issues.suggested_fix: Update founding partners list to include Google, Nvidia, and JPMorganChase. Remove 'Anthropic' from participant bullet or reframe as 'convened by Anthropic with partners including...'

issues.claim: Anthropic is limiting initial access to roughly 40 vetted organizations
issues.issue: The ~40 organizations are additional orgs beyond core Glasswing partners. Missing context: Anthropic committed $100M in model usage credits and $4M in open-source security donations.
issues.suggested_fix: Clarify 'more than 40 additional organizations beyond core partners.' Add $100M credit commitment as context.

issues.claim: No binding regulation has yet been issued in direct response to Mythos
issues.issue: Claim is unsourced but accurate as of April 12, 2026.
issues.suggested_fix: Add 'as of April 12, 2026, no formal regulatory action identified.'
